metadata.note: Command teardown of the ./setup script itself — the free-by-default readiness checker at the toolkit root. Bash 3.2-compatible (macOS-safe), built around a check() helper that eval-writes dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars instead of declare -A. Two verbs: bare './setup' (verify + FEATURE table + exit 0 iff all green) and './setup --install' (pip install requirements.txt + npm install runtime/remotion + copy bundled fonts + curl Kokoro model files from thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx releases — then verify). Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification — importing every Python dep, actually running ffmpeg/ffprobe, and synthesizing + decoding one real Kokoro phrase whose mean_volume must exceed -40 dB. Thirteen atomic checks aggregate into 7 FEATUREs; any missing atomic hint prints under the blocked feature. Unique-to-setup content vs the sibling doctor episode: the pip contract from requirements.txt (numpy>=2.0.2 pinning story), the four-phase --install pipeline, and the ElevenLabs guard at setup:102-115 (a paid-provider quarantine — the script exits 1 the day any of four fingerprints reappears in a file that isn't setup itself). All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation, section 3 captured with runtime/models temporarily unlinked to force one red row. No paid API, no upload, no network calls beyond the setup smoke test's local Kokoro synth. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged in README.md for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 cf8873d1a540147a49b11feff3dd4ab774fd4f0e0ef9941c52895bd691bb628c. beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the setup surface: verbatim shebang + short-help block + one honest sentence. Two modes end at the same seven-row table.
beats.narration_text: The setup script is the source of truth. Sixteen lines of header at the top: shebang, two modes, one honest sentence about what a green table proves. Bare dot slash setup verifies and prints the readiness table. Dot slash setup dash dash install installs the core Python dependencies, Remotion's node modules, the fonts, and the Kokoro model — then runs the same verification.

props.title: setup:1-16 — shebang + surface + one honest sentence
props.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup — the doctor for the brutalist toolkit (free by default).
#
#   ./setup            # check everything, print the readiness table
#   ./setup --install  # install the core Python deps + Remotion's node deps, then check
#
# Core features require no paid services or API keys. Everything below is free
# and local. Optional Higgsfield CLI login unlocks AI video beats; ElevenLabs is
# permanently removed. Exit 0 if all required features are ready; exit 1 otherwise.
#
# Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification below — importing every
# Python dep, actually running ffmpeg/ffprobe, and synthesizing + decoding
# one real Kokoro phrase (mean_volume > -40 dB). An install step's own exit
# code is reported (INSTALL_FAILED) but never substitutes for a check: a
# green table means the checks passed, not that `pip install` returned 0.
set -uo pipefail
props.sparkLine: Two modes. One script. One honest sentence.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK 2 — requirements.txt as the pip contract. Six pinning lines + the numpy>=2.0.2 rationale.
beats.narration_text: Under dash dash install, the whole Python surface comes from one file: requirements dot txt. Kokoro pinned at greater-than-or-equal zero point four — the free voice engine, no key. Mutagen at forty-seven for MP3 duration; that's the master clock. Pillow ten point two for slates. Manim eighteen for animation. Faster-whisper one for captions. And numpy pinned above two point zero point two, because Kokoro's release requires it, and Manim eighteen has no upper bound to fight. Six lines of pinning; that's the whole contract.

# brutalist — Python dependencies (free-only toolkit).
#   pip install -r requirements.txt
# numpy>=2.0.2 is required by kokoro-onnx (every >=0.4 release pins this
# floor); manim 0.18 and its deps have no upper bound on numpy, so there's
# no real conflict — just don't hold numpy below 2.

# ── core: audio-first narration pipeline ────────────────────────────────────
kokoro-onnx>=0.4            # the FREE voice engine (Kokoro-82M, local, no key)
mutagen>=1.47,<1.48         # audio-duration measurement (the master clock)
Pillow>=10.2,<11            # slates / request cards / previz / stills
numpy>=2.0.2

# ── animation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
manim>=0.18,<0.19           # pulls manimpango, moderngl, etc.
manimpango>=0.5,<0.6

# ── captions + word clock ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
faster-whisper>=1.0,<2      # forced alignment + transcript captions (local, no key)

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 1 — --install: four phases (pip, npm, fonts, Kokoro model). Every step's exit code is captured; no install turns a row green on its own.
beats.narration_text: Add dash dash install and setup does four things, in order, before it verifies. One: pip installs from requirements dot txt — break-system-packages first for the modern pip, plain second as a fallback. Two: change into runtime slash remotion and npm install. Three: copy the bundled fonts into the user font directory, and download Oswald from Google Fonts if it's missing. Four: only if the Kokoro model files are absent, curl them from the kokoro-onnx releases page. Every step's exit code is captured; every failure widens the fail path — but no install turns a row green on its own.

show.event: card in; title reads 'setup:57-100 — --install: four phases'

props.title: setup:57-100 — --install: four phases, then verify
props.code:
if [ "${1:-}" = "--install" ]; then
  # 1) pip: if/! pattern; --break-system-packages first, plain second
  b "Installing core Python deps…"; echo
  if ! python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages -r requirements.txt \
      && ! python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt; then
    r "Python dependency install FAILED"; INSTALL_FAILED=1
  fi; echo

  # 2) npm: Remotion's node deps
  b "Installing Remotion node deps…"; echo
  if ! (cd runtime/remotion && npm install); then
    r "npm install FAILED"; INSTALL_FAILED=1
  fi; echo

  # 3) fonts: bundled EB Garamond + download Oswald if missing
  b "Installing fonts into $(font_dir)…"; echo
  FONT_DIR="$(font_dir)"; mkdir -p "$FONT_DIR"
  find runtime/fonts -iname '*.ttf' -exec cp -n {} "$FONT_DIR/" \; 2>/dev/null
  if ! have_font "Oswald"; then
    curl -fsSL "https://…/Oswald%5Bwght%5D.ttf" \
      -o "$FONT_DIR/Oswald-Variable.ttf" || INSTALL_FAILED=1
  fi; have fc-cache && fc-cache -f >/dev/null 2>&1; echo

  # 4) Kokoro model: only if BOTH files are absent (~340 MB, one-time)
  if [ ! -f runtime/models/kokoro/kokoro-v1.0.onnx ] || \
     [ ! -f runtime/models/kokoro/voices-v1.0.bin ]; then
    b "Downloading the Kokoro voice model (~340MB)…"
    mkdir -p runtime/models/kokoro
    ( cd runtime/models/kokoro && curl -fLO …/kokoro-v1.0.onnx \
      && curl -fLO …/voices-v1.0.bin ) || INSTALL_FAILED=1
  fi; echo; shift || true
fi
# SAME live verification runs after. INSTALL_FAILED widens exit;
# it never turns a row green — that's the checks' job.
props.sparkLine: Four phases. Explicit error output. Then verify.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 2 — bash 3.2 compat. check() helper uses eval to write dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars instead of declare -A.
beats.narration_text: Under the hood, one small design choice makes this script portable. Macos ships bash three point two by default — no associative arrays. So instead of declaring an array, the check helper uses eval to write two dynamic variables per test: OK-underscore-ID and MISS-underscore-ID. That is why setup runs the same on a Mac and on Linux, without a bash five prerequisite.

show.event: card in; title reads 'setup:117-140 — check() and dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id>'
two example checks type below it

props.title: setup:117-140 — check() and dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id>
props.code:
# Dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars instead of associative arrays: macOS ships
# bash 3.2 by default (no `declare -A`), and this script must run there too.
check(){
  local id="$1"
  eval "OK_${id}=0"
  if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    eval "OK_${id}=1"
  else
    eval "MISS_${id}=\$3"
  fi
}

# Two examples — the first checks ffmpeg exists AND ffprobe exists;
# the second imports the Python module 'kokoro_onnx' from Python itself.
check ffmpeg    'ffmpeg -version >/dev/null 2>&1 && ffprobe -version >/dev/null 2>&1' \
                'install ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg / apt install ffmpeg)'
check py_kokoro 'pymod kokoro_onnx' 'pip install kokoro-onnx (the free voice engine)'

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 3 — live verification, not receipts. Kokoro must actually SPEAK a phrase above -40 dB to earn green.
beats.narration_text: Here is the part that makes the whole script honest. Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification. A successful pip install is not enough. For the audio feature to turn green, setup runs setup-underscore-smoke-underscore-kokoro dot py, which synthesizes one throwaway phrase and checks that the decoded audio's mean volume exceeds negative forty decibels. A silent wav is a failure. Kokoro has to actually speak to earn the green row.

show.event: card in; title reads 'live verification, not receipts'
the setup_smoke_kokoro.py summary types under it

props.title: live verification, not receipts
props.code:
# setup:137 — the kokoro_synth check row
check kokoro_synth \
  "python3 \"$HERE/runtime/scripts/setup_smoke_kokoro.py\"" \
  'Kokoro failed to synthesize + decode a test phrase above -40 dB —
   check model files, kokoro_onnx install, and ffmpeg
   (run runtime/scripts/setup_smoke_kokoro.py directly to see why)'

# What setup_smoke_kokoro.py actually does:
#   1. loads the onnx voice model from runtime/models/kokoro/
#   2. calls kokoro.create("This is a setup smoke test.", voice="af_bella")
#   3. writes the wav, then ffmpeg -af volumedetect decodes it
#   4. parses mean_volume, asserts it is greater than -40 dB

# From the top of setup, in plain English:
#   Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification below — importing
#   every Python dep, actually running ffmpeg/ffprobe, and synthesizing
#   + decoding one real Kokoro phrase (mean_volume > -40 dB). An install
#   step's own exit code is reported (INSTALL_FAILED) but never substitutes
#   for a check: a green table means the checks passed, not that
#   `pip install` returned 0.
props.sparkLine: Kokoro must actually speak. Silence fails.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 4 — the ElevenLabs guard (setup:102-115). A paid-provider quarantine that refuses to start if a fingerprint reappears in any file outside setup itself.
beats.narration_text: And one more design choice, unique to this script. Before any check runs, setup greps the whole toolkit for four fingerprints of a paid voice provider: the API-key environment variable, the domain, the engine string in a JSON, and the xi-api-key header. If any of them shows up in a file that isn't this setup script itself, the whole script exits one and lists the offending files. Free-by-default isn't a slogan; it's a guard that refuses to start the day the pattern comes back.

show.event: card in; title reads 'setup:102-115 — the ElevenLabs guard'

props.title: setup:102-115 — the ElevenLabs guard
props.code:
# ── ElevenLabs guard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Functional ElevenLabs references are bugs; prose documentation mentioning the
# name is allowed. setup is excluded because it contains this guard.
EL_PAT="ELEVEN""LABS_API_KEY|elevenlabs""\.io|\"engine\"[^\"]*\"elevenlabs\"|xi-api-key"
#      └──── four fingerprints, split so this line itself doesn't match ────┘

if grep -rqiE "$EL_PAT" \
    --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=__pycache__ \
    --exclude-dir='.claude' --exclude='CHANGELOG*' --exclude=setup .; then
  r "ElevenLabs reference found — this toolkit is Kokoro-only for narration."; echo
  echo "  Files with hits:"
  grep -rliE "$EL_PAT" \
    --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=__pycache__ \
    --exclude-dir='.claude' --exclude='CHANGELOG*' --exclude=setup . | sed 's/^/    /'
  exit 1
fi
props.sparkLine: Free-by-default is a guard, not a slogan.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — unlink runtime/models; audio row goes red with two hint lines; exit 1. Recovery: restore, or --install re-fetches. Verbatim from demo/RUN-LOG.txt sections 3 and 4.
beats.narration_text: One failure worth showing. Unlink the Kokoro model directory — the models are the one thing not in the git repo, because they're three hundred megabytes. Re-run setup. Audio row goes red. Two hint lines print underneath: the model files are missing, and the synth-and-decode phrase failed. Every other row stays green. Exit code: one. Recovery: put the files back — or on a fresh install, run setup with dash dash install and the fourth phase of the pipeline downloads them for you. The exit code is the whole point — a red row never ships a build.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — setup. A live-verification readiness checker, with an optional install-first mode. Two modes, one script, one seven-row table. It reads requirements dot txt for the pip contract, it makes Kokoro speak for the audio row, it refuses to run if a paid provider is smuggled in, and it exits zero only when every atomic check passes live. Run this before you fill a beat sheet, and downstream failures with cryptic messages become failures with a checklist.
